mainTopic: Whether a גוי's ownership removes the land's obligations, and whether owning a field's produce counts like owning the field (ביכורים)
overview: This amud finishes the גמרא's challenges to רבה, who holds that a גוי's purchase cannot free land in ארץ ישראל from מעשר. A ברייתא about a field shared by a Jew and a גוי seems to show that everyone agrees a גוי's share is exempt. The גמרא answers that the case is in סוריא, where כיבוש יחיד makes the land's holiness weaker. רב חייא בר אבין then challenges רבה from our משנה, which says a seller buys back the fruit and brings ביכורים only because of תיקון העולם. רב אשי answers that there were two rabbinic תקנות, first stopping the ביכורים and then putting them back. Next comes a dispute between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש: does someone who bought only a field's produce recite the ביכורים declaration? That depends on whether קנין פירות is like קנין הגוף. They argue back and forth using a husband who brings his wife's ביכורים. The amud ends as the גמרא begins showing that the two follow the same reasoning in another case, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The dispute between רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל about a shared field
steps.stepSummary: The end of the ברייתא about a field jointly owned by a Jew and a גוי: רבי says the produce is a mix of טבל and חולין, while רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the גוי's share is exempt and the Jew's share is obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: The produce of the shared field is considered untithed produce and non-sacred produce mixed together. This is רבי's view. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: the גוי's share is exempt, and the Jew's share is obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its quote of a ברייתא that it is using to challenge רבה. This quote sets up the next step, where the גמרא draws a conclusion from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both תנאים treat the גוי's portion as free from מעשר in some way. רבי calls it חולין mixed in with טבל, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל exempts the גוי's share outright. That shared assumption is what the גמרא will use against רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce from which תרומות and מעשרות have not yet been taken, so it may not be eaten
Ordinary, non-sacred produce with no obligation on it
Mixed together
Exempt / obligated

phrases.english: untithed produce and non-sacred produce are mixed with each other,
these are the words of Rabbi.
phrases.notes: "רבי" alone always means רבי יהודה הנשיא, the one who put together the משנה.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
the share of the gentile is exempt,
and the share of the Jew is obligated.

steps.triggerLanguage: טבל וחולין מעורבין זה בזה, דברי רבי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quotation of the ברייתא that the גמרא started before this section, as a challenge to רבה.
steps.raayaObject: רבה's rule that a גוי's ownership cannot remove the obligation of מעשר
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a field owned in partnership by a Jew and a גוי

steps.title: Both sides agree a גוי's ownership removes מעשר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל only disagree about ברירה, so both must agree that a גוי's ownership frees the land from מעשר. This contradicts רבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They only disagree about one thing. One master, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, holds that there is ברירה. The other master, רבי, holds that there is no ברירה. But everyone agrees that a גוי's purchase of land in ארץ ישראל has the power to remove it from the obligation of מעשר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out exactly what the two תנאים argue about. It then shows that the part they agree on goes against רבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their argument is only about ברירה: when the partners later divide the crop, do we say each side owned its share from the start? Neither side questions that the גוי's share is free of מעשר. That means both hold יש קנין לגוי להפקיע, which is the opposite of רבה's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Looking back after the fact: a later choice reveals what was true from the start
According to everyone
Ownership / acquisition
To remove or cancel (here, the obligation)
Tithe taken from produce

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the argument between רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is about a גוי's ownership. Their argument is only about ברירה. The point the גמרא uses against רבה is the thing they both agree on.

phrases.english: until here they only disagree
in that one master holds "there is retroactive clarification,"
phrases.notes: This "master" is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. Once the crop is divided, each partner's share counts as his from the start.

phrases.english: and one master holds "there is no retroactive clarification";
but according to everyone
a gentile has the power of acquisition in Eretz Yisrael
to remove it from the hand of the tithe!
phrases.notes: Literally "from the hand of tithe." It means taking the land out of the obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the challenge out of the ברייתא quoted in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's rule: אין קנין לגוי בארץ ישראל להפקיע מיד מעשר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The two תנאים only argue about ברירה. That means both assume the גוי's share is free of מעשר, which shows that a גוי's ownership does remove the obligation.

steps.title: The ברייתא is about סוריא, not ארץ ישראל proper
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is talking about a field in סוריא. That תנא holds כיבוש יחיד לא שמיה כיבוש, so a גוי's ownership can remove מעשר there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, the case is in סוריא. And this תנא holds that a conquest by an individual is not considered a real conquest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבה by limiting the ברייתא to סוריא. There the land's holiness is weaker, so a גוי's ownership can cancel the obligation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סוריא was conquered by דוד on his own initiative, not by the whole nation. If כיבוש יחיד is not a full conquest, the land is not fully holy, and a גוי's purchase can remove מעשר. רבה's rule still holds for real ארץ ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: Syria, lands conquered by דוד outside the borders of ארץ ישראל proper
A conquest done by an individual king rather than by the whole nation
Here too, using the same answer given earlier

steps.whatToRemember: This challenge, like the earlier one, is answered by saying the source is about סוריא, where כיבוש יחיד makes the holiness weaker. רבה's rule stays in place for ארץ ישראל proper.

phrases.english: here too it is in Syria;
and he holds that the conquest of an individual
is not called a conquest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2 by limiting the ברייתא to סוריא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא) to a special location
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is about ordinary ארץ ישראל, so it would contradict רבה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about סוריא, where כיבוש יחיד is not a real conquest. A גוי's ownership can remove מעשר only there.

steps.title: A new challenge from the ביכורים rule in our משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר אבין brings the משנה: someone who sold his field to a גוי buys back its fruit and brings ביכורים, but only because of תיקון העולם. That implies that by Torah law the גוי's ownership removed the obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בר אבין said: Come and hear. One who sells his field to a גוי must buy its fruit and bring ביכורים, because of תיקון העולם. Because of תיקון העולם, yes. But by Torah law, no!
steps.whatsHappening: רב חייא בר אבין opens a new attack on רבה, this time from our own משנה. He reads closely to show that the ביכורים obligation is only a rabbinic one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the field were still fully holy after the sale, the ביכורים would be a Torah obligation. The משנה needs to give a rabbinic reason, תיקון העולם, so by Torah law there is no obligation. That means the גוי's ownership removed the land's obligation, against רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the opening for bringing a proof or a challenge
First fruits brought to the בית המקדש
A rabbinic enactment for the good of society
By Torah law
He buys (here, he buys back the produce)

steps.whyThisMatters: This challenge comes from the משנה of this very perek, so it carries more weight. The סוריא answer is not used here. רב אשי answers it in a different way in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין, תָּא שְׁמַע:
phrases.english: Rav Ḥiyya bar Avin said: come and hear:
one who sells his field to a gentile
buys and brings first fruits
phrases.notes: He buys the fruit back from the גוי and brings it as ביכורים.

phrases.english: because of the betterment of the world.
because of the betterment of the world, yes,
by Torah law, no!

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב חייא בר אבין, תא שמע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא challenge was answered, a new challenge against רבה starts from the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's rule: אין קנין לגוי להפקיע מיד מעשר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה gives ביכורים only a rabbinic reason. That implies there is no Torah obligation, so a גוי's ownership must remove the land's holiness.

steps.title: Two back-and-forth enactments about ביכורים
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that there were two rabbinic תקנות. First the חכמים stopped people from bringing ביכורים from land sold to a גוי, and later they told them to bring again. The משנה's 'תיקון העולם' refers to that second enactment.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: There were two enactments. At first, people brought ביכורים from such land by Torah law. When the חכמים saw that people were selling land to גוים casually, because they thought the land stays holy anyway, the חכמים enacted that they should not bring. Later they saw that anyone who could not make ends meet sold his land anyway, and the fields stayed stuck in the hands of גוים. So they went back and enacted that they should bring.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the challenge from the משנה. He says the words 'because of תיקון העולם' describe the last of two rabbinic enactments, not a change from the Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that 'תיקון העולם' means that by Torah law there is no ביכורים obligation. רב אשי shows a different history. By Torah law they brought from the start, the חכמים stopped it so people would not think selling to a גוי is harmless, and then brought it back so the seller would feel pressure to buy the field back. So the משנה gives no proof against רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic enactment
By Torah law
They remain in their holiness
He cannot manage, meaning he is too poor to get by
They become stuck, meaning the fields are lost for good

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's 'תיקון העולם' refers to the second rabbinic enactment, which put back the bringing of ביכורים. It does not show that a גוי's ownership cancels the obligation by Torah law.
steps.confusionAlert: Both enactments are rabbinic. The first stopped the bringing and the second put it back. The original Torah-level practice was to bring ביכורים.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
There were two enactments.
Originally, they would bring [ביכורים] by Torah law.
Once [the חכמים] saw that people would casually sell [their land to גוים],
because they thought the lands stay in their holiness,
they enacted for them that they should not bring.

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דַּחֲזוֹ דְּמַאן דְּלָא סַגִּי לֵיהּ – מְזַבֵּן,
phrases.english: Once they saw that whoever could not get by would sell anyway,
and the fields were getting stuck in the hands of גוים,
they went back and enacted that they should bring.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: שְׁתֵּי תַּקָּנוֹת הֲווֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב חייא בר אבין's challenge from the משנה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the source by giving the history of the rabbinic enactments
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Because of תיקון העולם' means that by Torah law the גוי's ownership removed the ביכורים obligation
steps.terutzMaskana: The phrase refers to the second rabbinic enactment that put the bringing back. Torah law always required bringing, so there is no contradiction to רבה
steps.whyThisMatters: It removes the last challenge against רבה in this section and shows that a rabbinic 'תיקון' can reverse an earlier rabbinic rule.

steps.title: Selling a field only for its produce
steps.stepSummary: A new dispute: when someone sells only the produce rights of his field, רבי יוחנן says the buyer brings ביכורים and recites the declaration, and ריש לקיש says he brings but does not recite.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: Someone sells his field only for its produce. רבי יוחנן says the buyer brings ביכורים and recites. ריש לקיש says he brings but does not recite.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with an אמוראים dispute about a buyer who owns the produce of a field but not the field itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that the buyer brings ביכורים. They argue only about the קריאה, the declaration that thanks ה' for 'the land You gave me.' The question is whether this buyer can say that about land he does not fully own.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated, which introduces a dispute between אמוראים
For its produce only
He brings ביכורים and recites the declaration
And he does not recite

phrases.english: It was stated:
One who sells his field for its produce,
phrases.notes: He keeps the land itself and sells only the right to everything that grows on it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says: He brings and recites.
phrases.notes: The reading is the ביכורים declaration, דברים 26:5-10.

phrases.aramaic: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: מֵבִיא וְאֵינוֹ קוֹרֵא.
phrases.english: Reish Lakish says: He brings and does not recite.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new, related discussion about ownership and ביכורים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן says the buyer of the produce brings and recites. ריש לקיש says he brings but does not recite.

steps.title: The reasoning: is owning the produce like owning the land?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the dispute. רבי יוחנן holds that owning the produce counts like owning the land itself, and ריש לקיש holds that it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says he brings and recites because owning the produce is like owning the land itself. ריש לקיש says he brings and does not recite because owning the produce is not like owning the land itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the principle behind each side of the dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, someone who owns everything the field produces is treated like the owner of the field, so he can honestly say 'the land You gave me.' For ריש לקיש, the land still belongs to the seller, so the buyer cannot make that declaration.

keyTerms.meaning: Ownership of the produce only
Ownership of the item itself, here the land
Is considered like

steps.whatToRemember: The dispute between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש depends on whether קנין פירות is like קנין הגוף.
steps.whyThisMatters: The question of whether קנין פירות counts like קנין הגוף comes up all over ש"ס, and here it is tied to the ביכורים declaration.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says he brings and recites
because ownership of the produce is like ownership of the item itself.

phrases.aramaic: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר מֵבִיא וְאֵינוֹ קוֹרֵא –
phrases.english: Reish Lakish says he brings and does not recite

phrases.aramaic: קִנְיַן פֵּירוֹת לָאו כְּקִנְיַן הַגּוּף דָּמֵי.
phrases.english: because ownership of the produce is not like ownership of the item itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר מֵבִיא וְקוֹרֵא – קִנְיַן פֵּירוֹת כְּקִנְיַן הַגּוּף דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the dispute in step 6
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן holds that קנין פירות is like קנין הגוף. ריש לקיש holds that it is not.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן challenges ריש לקיש from a man bringing his wife's first fruits
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן cites the ברייתא that a man brings his wife's ביכורים and recites, even though he owns only the produce of her field.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן challenged ריש לקיש: the פסוק says 'and to your house.' This teaches that a man brings his wife's ביכורים and recites the declaration.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן challenges ריש לקיש with a ברייתא. It says a husband brings his wife's ביכורים and also recites the declaration.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A husband owns only the produce of his wife's field, not the field itself. Yet the ברייתא says he recites. This seems to prove רבי יוחנן's view that owning the produce counts like owning the land, against ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection against him from an authoritative source
'And to your house'. Here it is read as meaning one's wife.
His wife's first fruits, which grow from the field she owns
And he recites the ביכורים declaration (מקרא ביכורים)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan raised an objection to Reish Lakish:
"And to your house": this teaches
phrases.notes: דברים 26:11. Here 'your house' is read as meaning your wife.

phrases.english: that a man brings his wife's first fruits, and he recites.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the dispute explained in Step 7 against a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that owning only the produce does not count like owning the land
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A husband owns only the produce of his wife's field, yet he recites. So owning the produce must count like owning the land.

steps.title: ריש לקיש answers that the wife's case is a special verse
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers that the wife's case is different, because the פסוק explicitly includes 'your house'.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said to him: it is different there, because it is written 'and to your house.'
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש defends himself. He says the wife's field is a special case that the פסוק itself adds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reciting for a wife's field comes from a special word in the פסוק, not from a general rule about owning produce. So we cannot learn from it that every owner of produce recites.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there; that case is an exception
Because it is written in the פסוק

phrases.english: He said to him: It is different there,
since it is written: "And to your house."

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source to an exception created by the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The wife's case shows that owning produce always counts like owning the land.
steps.terutzMaskana: The wife's case is a special rule from the word 'ולביתך'. It does not apply to other cases of owning only the produce.

steps.title: Second version: ריש לקיש uses the same source against רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: In another version, ריש לקיש cites the ברייתא of 'ולביתך' to challenge רבי יוחנן. The פסוק had to add the wife's case, so in general someone who owns only the produce does not recite.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say it went the other way: ריש לקיש challenged רבי יוחנן. 'And to your house' teaches that a man brings his wife's ביכורים and recites. That is only there, because the פסוק says 'and to your house.' In general, someone who owns only the produce does not recite!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the exchange. This time ריש לקיש is the one who quotes the ברייתא, and he uses it to attack רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש reasons that the פסוק needed a special word to include the wife's field. That shows that without it, owning only the produce would not be enough to recite. So the special case proves the general rule goes against רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: And there are those who say. This introduces a different version of the same discussion.
The full name of ריש לקיש
In general; in ordinary cases

steps.confusionAlert: Both versions use the exact same ברייתא, but the roles flip. In the first version רבי יוחנן uses it as a challenge. In the second, ריש לקיש uses it as a challenge. Watch who is speaking.

phrases.english: And there are those who say:

phrases.aramaic: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish raised an objection to Rabbi Yochanan:
"And to your house": this teaches
that a man brings his wife's first fruits and recites.
There it is so, because it is written "and to your house,"
but in general, no!
phrases.notes: He means that in ordinary cases, someone who owns only the produce would not recite.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different version of the exchange in Steps 8 and 9, with the roles reversed.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's view that owning the produce counts like owning the land
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק needed a special word to include the wife's field. That shows the general rule is that owning only the produce is not enough to recite.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן says this verse is the source of his rule
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the פסוק of 'ולביתך' is exactly the source of his own general rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said to him: I also learn my reason from this very place.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers ריש לקיש's challenge. He says the wife's case is not an exception at all. It is where his rule comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש sees 'ולביתך' as a special exception. רבי יוחנן sees it as the model for every case: a husband owns only the produce, so anyone who owns only the produce is treated like the owner of the land.

keyTerms.meaning: My own reason
Also; too
From here; from this source

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree a husband brings and recites for his wife's field. They disagree about whether that פסוק is a one-time exception (ריש לקיש) or the source of a general rule (רבי יוחנן).

phrases.english: He said to him: My reason, too,
I say it from here.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: טַעְמָא דִּידִי נָמֵי מֵהָכָא קָאָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers ריש לקיש's challenge in Step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the same source the opposite way: as the basis of the rule, not an exception
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The wife's case is a special exception, which shows that owning only the produce does not usually count.
steps.terutzMaskana: The wife's case is the source that teaches owning the produce counts like owning the land in every case.

steps.title: ריש לקיש challenges from the man whose wife died on the way
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש cites a ברייתא: a man traveling with his wife's ביכורים who hears she died brings and recites. That implies that if she had not died, he would not recite.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש challenged him: if a man was on the road with his wife's ביכורים in his hand, and he heard that his wife died, he brings and recites. So if she died, yes. If she did not die, no!
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש brings a new ברייתא against רבי יוחנן. He makes an inference from its wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says he recites because his wife died. Once she dies, he inherits the field itself. That suggests that while she was alive, owning only the produce would not have been enough to recite, which goes against רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Traveling on the road, here on the way to bring ביכורים
In his hand; in his possession
If she died, yes; if she did not die, no. This is an inference drawn from the wording.

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:
phrases.notes: Here ריש לקיש is the one challenging רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: If he was traveling on the road

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ: הָיָה בָּא בַּדֶּרֶךְ וּבִיכּוּרֵי אִשְׁתּוֹ בְּיָדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבי יוחנן defends his reading of 'ולביתך', ריש לקיש brings a new source against him.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's view that owning the produce counts like owning the land
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He recites only because she died and he now owns the land. So while she was alive, owning only the produce would not have been enough to recite.

steps.title: The wife's death is mentioned only to block a possible decree
steps.stepSummary: The husband brings and recites even if his wife did not die. The ברייתא mentions her death only because we might have thought to make a decree based on רבי יוסי בר חנינא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The same law holds even if she did not die. But the ברייתא needed to mention that she died, because you might have thought we should make a decree because of רבי יוסי בר חנינא's rule.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers ריש לקיש's challenge from step 12. The ברייתא's mention of 'she died' does not mean he would fail to recite if she were alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש had inferred that while the wife is alive, the husband does not recite. The answer is that he recites either way. 'She died' is mentioned only because her death might seem to cause a new problem, which the next step explains.

keyTerms.meaning: the same law applies
it was necessary for it to say
you might have thought to say
let us make a rabbinic decree

steps.confusionAlert: The death of the wife is not what allows him to recite. It is mentioned only because her death might have seemed to cause a problem.

steps.title: One person must both take and bring the ביכורים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר חנינא rules that if a messenger dies on the way, someone else brings the fruit but does not recite, since one person must do both the taking and the bringing. The ברייתא teaches that we do not apply this to the husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר חנינא said: if someone harvested his ביכורים, sent them with a messenger, and the messenger died on the way, the fruit is brought but the פסוקים are not recited. The פסוק says 'and you shall take' and 'and you shall bring,' so one person must do both. The ברייתא comes to teach us that this does not apply to the husband.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי יוסי בר חנינא's rule to explain the decree it worried about. It then closes the answer: the ברייתא teaches us that no such decree applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband took the fruit while his wife was alive, when he owned only the produce. He brought it after she died, when he owned the field. This looks like the taking and the bringing were done by two different 'owners,' like the messenger case. The ברייתא teaches that he still recites, because owning the produce already counts like owning the field.

keyTerms.meaning: messenger or agent
he brings the fruit but does not recite the פסוקים
taking (separating) and bringing
it teaches us

steps.whatToRemember: According to this answer, owning the produce counts like owning the field. That is why the husband's status did not change when his wife died, and he recites.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer removes ריש לקיש's last proof, so רבי יוחנן's position stands.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina said:
If he harvested them and sent them with a messenger,
and the messenger died on the way,
he brings them but does not recite,
as it is stated: 'And you shall take' and 'and you shall bring,'
not until the taking and bringing are done by one person;
so it teaches us.
phrases.notes: This finishes the answer from step 13: the ברייתא mentions 'she died' to teach that we do not make that decree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the rule behind the decree mentioned in step 13, then completes that answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If a messenger dies on the way, the ביכורים are brought but the פסוקים are not recited, because one person must both take and bring them. The ברייתא shows that the husband still recites.

steps.title: The same two opinions appear in the case of selling a field
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש keep to their own reasoning about owning the produce, in another dispute that begins 'one who sells his field.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And they follow their own reasoning, as it was stated: one who sells his field...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is starting to show a second dispute where the same two אמוראים argue in the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא connects this debate to another dispute between them, about selling a field. This shows that their views on owning the produce are consistent. The details of that case continue on the next amud.
